To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The brain of the reader has a different organization than the brain of the pre- reader, and this difference is due to learning to read, not to the genetic or biological factors.

(1) reading and language are related, (2) reading is a complex cognitive skill that involves multiple brain regions and networks, (3) the brain is malleable and changes in response to reading instruction and reading practice.
The development of language comprehension and reading is supported by the same brain regions, and that these regions show similar developmental trajectories.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and use of language, and the neural systems that support it.
the development of language and reading in children, the role of phonological awareness, and the impact of a stimulating Home Literate Environment.
how learning to read impacts on a child's brain, and how a Home Literacy Environment can influence the development of reading.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Home Literacy Environment is a key factor for children to learn to read.

the development of reading is a complex interaction of biological systems (genetics, brain, sensory and motor systems), environmental influences (Home Literacy Environment) and the interaction between them.
reading is a skill which is dependent upon the interaction of the child, their biological systems, their Home Literacy Environment, and the school system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
children with dyslexia have a deficit in the neural systems that are responsible for the phonological processing of speech.

the Home Literacy Environment is the most important factor in determining reading ability, and that the Home Literate Environment is more important than oral language skills in determining the ability to read.
the development of reading skills is dependent on a combination of biological and environmental influences.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Home Literacy Environment is an important factor for reading comprehension.
reading acquisition is a complex process that involves the interaction of biological and environmental factors.

reading is a complex process involving a range of skills, including phonological awareness, rapid naming, and vocabulary, and that the neural networks supporting these skills are not fully mature until late adolescence.
